description: What a context window is made of: the system prompt, the tools, the memory, the files, the conversation and the tool results, measured against the model's budget. The presentation (Variant) changes only the PICTURE — one stacked bar (the default), a hundred cells over the budget so the free headroom is visible, or the core TmChart treemap. Every picture is decorative (aria-hidden); the legend table under it is the representation a reader, a screen reader and a copy/paste get, and it carries the label, the tokens, the whole percentage and the localized Required / Summarized / Omitted words of every section — never a colour-only cue. The total is a single role="meter" element carrying the invariant machine values and a localized aria-valuetext, so the amount is heard once (the visible read-out above it is sighted-only duplication). The percentages of the sections come from the largest-remainder split (ContextUsageMath.Shares), so they add up to exactly 100 %; a section with tokens whose rounded share is zero reads "< 1 %" and still paints a visible sliver. A section with Items expands into its entries through a native disclosure button, and a removable section or entry offers the localized Remove action. The component NEVER edits the snapshot: it reports the reader's intent through OnRemoveItem (the whole section when ContextUsageRemoval.Item is null, one entry otherwise) and OnCompact, and the host decides what to do; because the pressed control can disappear with the removal, the focus is handed back to the section's own disclosure button — or to the component root when that is gone too. The component is transport-agnostic and declares no motion at all: it renders the snapshot it is given and never polls. The ONE polite live region announces a budget CROSSING only, so a page load stays silent.

examples.title: A context window a host measures
examples.code:
<TmContextUsage Snapshot="@snapshot"
                Title="Context window"
                OnRemoveItem="OnRemoveAsync"
                OnCompact="CompactAsync" />

@code {
    private ContextUsageSnapshot snapshot = new()
    {
        BudgetTokens = 16_000,
        CacheHit = 0.62,
        Sections =
        [
            new("system", "System prompt") { Kind = ContextUsageKind.System, Tokens = 1_200, IsRequired = true },
            new("files", "Files")
            {
                Kind = ContextUsageKind.Files,
                Tokens = 5_000,
                CanRemove = true,
                Items = [new ContextUsageItem("contract", "Contract.pdf") { Tokens = 4_000, CanRemove = true }],
            },
            new("chat", "Chat history") { Kind = ContextUsageKind.Chat, Tokens = 6_000 },
        ],
    };

    private Task OnRemoveAsync(ContextUsageRemoval removal)
    {
        // removal.Item is null for a whole section, otherwise it names the single entry.
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }

    private Task CompactAsync() => Task.CompletedTask;
}

parameters.name: Snapshot
parameters.description: The snapshot to render — the budget, the sections and the cache-hit share. Null (or a snapshot with no sections) renders the localized empty state instead of an empty chart. The component never mutates it and never polls: a host pushes a new instance as the conversation grows.

parameters.name: Variant
parameters.description: How the context is presented. Default ContextUsageVariant.Bar (one stacked bar); the grid shows a hundred cells over the budget and the treemap draws the sections through the core TmChart. The legend table, the meter and the empty state are identical in every variant.

parameters.name: OnRemoveItem
parameters.description: Raised when the reader asks to drop something: something reported by a section with ContextUsageSection.CanRemove (the whole section — ContextUsageRemoval.Item is null) or an entry with ContextUsageItem.CanRemove. The action is rendered only when this callback is bound, so a read-only host offers no removal at all.

parameters.name: OnCompact
parameters.description: Raised when the reader asks for a compaction (summarise the optional parts). The action is rendered only when this callback is bound, and it is DISABLED while no section can be compacted (ContextUsageMath.IsCompactable), so a button is never offered that would do nothing.

parameters.name: Title
parameters.description: The visible heading of the panel and, through aria-labelledby, the name of the meter. Null renders no heading; the panel and the meter are then named by AriaLabel or the localized default.

parameters.name: ShowTitle
parameters.description: Whether the heading is rendered. Default true; a host that already titles the card passes false and keeps naming the meter by AriaLabel or the localized default.

parameters.name: HeadingLevel
parameters.description: The heading's level in the page outline, clamped to 2–6. Default 3. The heading is only rendered when Title is set and ShowTitle is true.

parameters.name: AriaLabel
parameters.description: The accessible name used when no visible heading names the panel, and the panel root's name. Null falls back to the localized "Context usage". A rendered Title always wins for the meter, so one control never carries two names.

parameters.name: Culture
parameters.description: The culture that formats the token counts and the percentages. Null means the current culture at render time. The machine-readable attributes (aria-valuenow / aria-valuemax) are always invariant — a culture's group separator would change the value a screen reader reads.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.
